experiment.hypothesis: Standard PyTorch F.kl_div computes KL divergence via cancellation-prone log-space subtraction, causing negative outputs in FP16/BF16/FP32 on nearby distributions typical of RLHF/GRPO trust regions. We demonstrate that this pathology extends directly to the backward pass — creating up to ~50% silent gradient dead-zones under naive clamp(min=0) patches and severe reverse-KL gradient corruption — while naive Schulman k3 suffers both small-|d| underflow and large-|d| FP16 NaN overflow. We derive an overflow-free two-branch 6th-order Bregman-Taylor identity with cancellation-free analytic gradients and implement a fused Blackwell Triton forward/backward kernel benchmarked up to frontier LLM vocabularies (V=151,936) and 3-seed BF16 RLHF policy optimization (V=32,000).

analysis.abstract_text: Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence regularization is foundational to modern reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), and logit distillation over large vocabularies (V = 32,000-151,936). Yet standard PyTorch F.kl_div evaluates sum_i p_i (log p_i - log q_i), suffering catastrophic cancellation whenever policy and reference distributions lie within typical trust-region proximity. Extending prior forward-pass observations across 36 regimes (forward and reverse KL; FP16, BF16, FP32; eps in [1e-4, 1e-1]), we show this pathology corrupts the backward pass directly: naive F.kl_div produces negative KL on up to 50.4% of inputs and 39.2% reverse-KL gradient sign flips (BF16, eps=1e-2); the common clamp(min=0) patch eliminates negative scalars only by inducing up to 50.4% silent zero-gradient dead-zones (61.8% sign flips); and naive BF16 Schulman k3 (exp(d)-1-d) suffers 100% premature zeroing for eps <= 1e-2. We derive an overflow-free two-branch 6th-order Bregman-Taylor formulation with cancellation-free analytic gradients and implement a fused Blackwell Triton forward/backward kernel that streams online logsumexp in FP32 registers without materializing (N, V) FP32 intermediates. On an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, our kernel achieves 0.0% negative KL across all 36 regimes (Wilcoxon p=1.45e-11), cuts FP32 (eps=1e-4) relative error from 21.1 to 1.42e-04 (149,111x reduction), runs 6.52x faster with 80.0% less peak VRAM than FP32-upcast F.kl_div at Qwen3 V=151,936 (30.4x faster than eager Bregman-Taylor), and matches the FP32 oracle exactly in 3-seed BF16 RLHF policy optimization (V=32,000) where clamped F.kl_div collapses into negative true objective (-0.00162 vs. +0.00164) with 99.4% dead-KL steps.
findings: Forward & backward gradient corruption across 36 regimes (Wilcoxon p=1.45e-11): PyTorch F.kl_div returns negative values on up to 50.4% of inputs and corrupts BF16 reverse-KL gradients (eps=1e-2) with 39.1% sign flips (cos=0.589). Clamping F.kl_div.clamp(min=0) induces 50.4% silent zero-gradient dead-zones and 61.8% sign flips (cos=0.371).

Even in FP32 (eps=1e-4), F.kl_div and FP32-upcast yield 48.1% negative outputs and median relative error 21.14 (2,114%); our 6th-order Bregman-Taylor branch cuts median error by 149,111x to 1.42e-04 (0.0% negative, 0.0% error >=1%).

Blackwell RTX 5090 Triton scaling at frontier LLM vocabularies (Qwen3 V=151,936, N=512, BF16 fwd+bwd): Fused Triton Bregman-Taylor runs in 0.90 ms using 296.8 MB extra VRAM — 6.52x faster with 80.0% less VRAM than FP32-upcast F.kl_div (5.87 ms, 1483.8 MB) and 30.4x faster than eager PyTorch Bregman-Taylor (27.32 ms, 4822.2 MB).

Downstream 3-seed BF16 RLHF/GRPO policy optimization (V=32,000, beta=2.0): Fused Triton matches the FP32 oracle identically (true objective +0.00164, true KL 0.00069, 0.000 median KL error), whereas clamped F.kl_div collapses to negative objective (-0.00162, 5.7x excess KL drift, 99.4% dead-KL steps) and BF16 F.kl_div / Schulman k3 plateau ~19% suboptimal (+0.00134 / +0.00132).

limitations: Irreducible input quantization floor: if logits are rounded to BF16 prior to the kernel call with |z_q - z_p| < 0.5 ULP_BF16, sub-ULP differences are already lost before KL evaluation (matching FP32-upcast ceiling).
Evaluated on full-vocabulary categorical KL (V up to 151,936); sampled-token Monte Carlo GRPO benefits primarily from scalar Eq. (1) stabilization.
Continuous exponential-family KL divergences require family-specific cancellation-free identities.
